propositions: Write-op input surfaces across lib/CLI/MCP adapters are hand-mirrored with no mechanical guard against parameter drift; changes on one adapter can silently omit params on another (e.g., force/reason/caused_by/ref on MCP transition/claim).

A single conformance-oracle contract table (one row per test case) drives behavioral execution through all three adapters against a fresh store; any divergence in ACCEPTED/REJECTED classification or rule-identity fails the suite, catching both missing params and runtime conditional-rule drift.

The oracle encodes current MCP reason/caused_by/force gaps as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago; when that ticket lands, the strict-xfail flips to xpass, forcing marker removal and signaling convergence.

Runtime conditional rules (close_class required, reason required for REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES) are asserted behaviorally — the contract includes rows that are consistently REJECTED across all three adapters, proving the rule holds uniformly.

Adapter-bound internals (source, return_alias, _creation_channel, repo_root) are excluded from the contract to prevent false divergences; a negative-control row confirms they produce no spurious failures.

The oracle reuses and extends the existing three-adapter harness (Adapter protocol, Outcome, Library/CLI/MCP implementations) rather than building fresh drivers, threading force/reason/close_class/caused_by/ref through the shared transport layer.
